name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Example app pub get
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter pub get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

blocks.text:
# Weekly test-shard rebalancer (issue #177, AC3/E4): re-splits the unit-test
# shards from downloaded JUnit timing artifacts when available (file counts
# otherwise) and commits scripts/test_shards.json back to main ONLY when the
# skew improved or the manifest was missing.
name: Shard rebalance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rebalance:
    name: Rebalance test shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # secrets.* is not allowed in job-level `if:`, so the PAT is exported as
    # an env var and the push step below skips itself gracefully when empty.
    env:
      RELEASE_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed manifest triggers downstream
          # workflows; an unset secret falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN here and the
          # push step skips itself.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # Timing artifacts come from recent successful CI runs on main; their
      # absence is fine — the rebalancer then falls back to file counts.
      # Core (junit-shard-*) and fa_ui (junit-faui-shard-*, issue #283)
      # timings are split into separate dirs so same-named suite paths can
      # never cross-contaminate the other's weights.
      - name: Download recent JUnit timing artifacts (best effort)
        id: timings
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .shard-timings .timings-core .timings-faui
          for id in $(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main \
              --status success --limit 5 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
            gh run download "$id" --dir ".shard-timings/$id" \
              --pattern '*junit*' 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          find .shard-timings -name '*.xml' | while read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              *junit-faui-shard-*) cp "$f" ".timings-faui/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
              *junit-shard-*)      cp "$f" ".timings-core/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
            esac
          done
          for pkg in core faui; do
            if find ".timings-$pkg" -name '*.xml' -print -quit | grep -q .; then
              echo "mode-$pkg=junit" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            else
              echo "mode-$pkg=filecount" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          done

      # Skew is measured over WEIGHTS (summed meta.weights per shard — real
      # test durations once junit artifacts exist, file counts before), not
      # unit counts: counting units said nothing about balance (issue #194
      # pt 1). Units missing from weights (brand-new dirs) count as 1.0.
      # Both manifests are measured (core + fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Skew before rebalance
        id: before
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"skew-core={skew('scripts/test_shards.json')}")
          print(f"skew-faui={skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF

      - name: Run the rebalancer
        run: |
          # Core is file-level ×4 (test/cli was half the suite as a single
          # dir-unit — undivisible; see ci.yml test-core comment).
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-core }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit .timings-core \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          else
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          fi
          # fa_ui (issue #283): flat layout → file-level units; goldens are
          # host-locked and stay out of the shards. Units are stored
          # relative to packages/fa_ui (same convention as core's test/).
          cd packages/fa_ui
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-faui }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit ../../.timings-faui \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          else
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          fi

      # Commit only when a manifest was missing or the skew (max shard
      # size / mean shard size) strictly improved for EITHER suite (core
      # or fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Decide whether to commit
        id: decide
        run: |
          after=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"{skew('scripts/test_shards.json')} {skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF
          )
          after_core=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f1)
          after_faui=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f2)
          before_core="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-core }}"
          before_faui="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-faui }}"
          echo "skew core: before=$before_core after=$after_core"
          echo "skew faui: before=$before_faui after=$after_faui"
          improved() {
            [ "$1" = "missing" ] && return 0
            [ "$2" != "missing" ] && \
              awk -v a="$2" -v b="$1" 'BEGIN{exit !(a < b)}'
          }
          if improved "$before_core" "$after_core" || \
             improved "$before_faui" "$after_faui"; then
            echo "commit=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "commit=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Commit and push rebalanced manifest to main
        if: steps.decide.outputs.commit == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -z "$RELEASE_PAT" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured; skipping push of shard manifests"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "418982+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add scripts/test_shards.json scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Manifest unchanged; nothing to push."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(ci): rebalance test shards (issues #177, #283)"
          git push origin HEAD:main

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

      # AC4 (REG): the checker must reject a @v4 fixture, a 40-char NON-hex
      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null

How to prepare a release

  1. Switch to a new branch from main.

  3. Update the version in https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/package.json.

  8. Commit your changes and push your branch upstream.
  9. Open a pull request against main and get it reviewed and merged.
  10. Draft a new release https://github.com/actions/cache/releases use the same version number used in package.json
    1. Create a new tag with the version number.

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Example app pub get
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter pub get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

blocks.text:
# Weekly test-shard rebalancer (issue #177, AC3/E4): re-splits the unit-test
# shards from downloaded JUnit timing artifacts when available (file counts
# otherwise) and commits scripts/test_shards.json back to main ONLY when the
# skew improved or the manifest was missing.
name: Shard rebalance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rebalance:
    name: Rebalance test shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # secrets.* is not allowed in job-level `if:`, so the PAT is exported as
    # an env var and the push step below skips itself gracefully when empty.
    env:
      RELEASE_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed manifest triggers downstream
          # workflows; an unset secret falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN here and the
          # push step skips itself.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # Timing artifacts come from recent successful CI runs on main; their
      # absence is fine — the rebalancer then falls back to file counts.
      # Core (junit-shard-*) and fa_ui (junit-faui-shard-*, issue #283)
      # timings are split into separate dirs so same-named suite paths can
      # never cross-contaminate the other's weights.
      - name: Download recent JUnit timing artifacts (best effort)
        id: timings
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .shard-timings .timings-core .timings-faui
          for id in $(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main \
              --status success --limit 5 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
            gh run download "$id" --dir ".shard-timings/$id" \
              --pattern '*junit*' 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          find .shard-timings -name '*.xml' | while read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              *junit-faui-shard-*) cp "$f" ".timings-faui/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
              *junit-shard-*)      cp "$f" ".timings-core/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
            esac
          done
          for pkg in core faui; do
            if find ".timings-$pkg" -name '*.xml' -print -quit | grep -q .; then
              echo "mode-$pkg=junit" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            else
              echo "mode-$pkg=filecount" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          done

      # Skew is measured over WEIGHTS (summed meta.weights per shard — real
      # test durations once junit artifacts exist, file counts before), not
      # unit counts: counting units said nothing about balance (issue #194
      # pt 1). Units missing from weights (brand-new dirs) count as 1.0.
      # Both manifests are measured (core + fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Skew before rebalance
        id: before
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"skew-core={skew('scripts/test_shards.json')}")
          print(f"skew-faui={skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF

      - name: Run the rebalancer
        run: |
          # Core is file-level ×4 (test/cli was half the suite as a single
          # dir-unit — undivisible; see ci.yml test-core comment).
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-core }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit .timings-core \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          else
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          fi
          # fa_ui (issue #283): flat layout → file-level units; goldens are
          # host-locked and stay out of the shards. Units are stored
          # relative to packages/fa_ui (same convention as core's test/).
          cd packages/fa_ui
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-faui }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit ../../.timings-faui \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          else
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          fi

      # Commit only when a manifest was missing or the skew (max shard
      # size / mean shard size) strictly improved for EITHER suite (core
      # or fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Decide whether to commit
        id: decide
        run: |
          after=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"{skew('scripts/test_shards.json')} {skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF
          )
          after_core=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f1)
          after_faui=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f2)
          before_core="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-core }}"
          before_faui="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-faui }}"
          echo "skew core: before=$before_core after=$after_core"
          echo "skew faui: before=$before_faui after=$after_faui"
          improved() {
            [ "$1" = "missing" ] && return 0
            [ "$2" != "missing" ] && \
              awk -v a="$2" -v b="$1" 'BEGIN{exit !(a < b)}'
          }
          if improved "$before_core" "$after_core" || \
             improved "$before_faui" "$after_faui"; then
            echo "commit=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "commit=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Commit and push rebalanced manifest to main
        if: steps.decide.outputs.commit == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -z "$RELEASE_PAT" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured; skipping push of shard manifests"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "418982+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add scripts/test_shards.json scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Manifest unchanged; nothing to push."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(ci): rebalance test shards (issues #177, #283)"
          git push origin HEAD:main

      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Example app pub get
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter pub get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

blocks.text:
# Weekly test-shard rebalancer (issue #177, AC3/E4): re-splits the unit-test
# shards from downloaded JUnit timing artifacts when available (file counts
# otherwise) and commits scripts/test_shards.json back to main ONLY when the
# skew improved or the manifest was missing.
name: Shard rebalance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rebalance:
    name: Rebalance test shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # secrets.* is not allowed in job-level `if:`, so the PAT is exported as
    # an env var and the push step below skips itself gracefully when empty.
    env:
      RELEASE_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed manifest triggers downstream
          # workflows; an unset secret falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN here and the
          # push step skips itself.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # Timing artifacts come from recent successful CI runs on main; their
      # absence is fine — the rebalancer then falls back to file counts.
      # Core (junit-shard-*) and fa_ui (junit-faui-shard-*, issue #283)
      # timings are split into separate dirs so same-named suite paths can
      # never cross-contaminate the other's weights.
      - name: Download recent JUnit timing artifacts (best effort)
        id: timings
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .shard-timings .timings-core .timings-faui
          for id in $(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main \
              --status success --limit 5 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
            gh run download "$id" --dir ".shard-timings/$id" \
              --pattern '*junit*' 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          find .shard-timings -name '*.xml' | while read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              *junit-faui-shard-*) cp "$f" ".timings-faui/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
              *junit-shard-*)      cp "$f" ".timings-core/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
            esac
          done
          for pkg in core faui; do
            if find ".timings-$pkg" -name '*.xml' -print -quit | grep -q .; then
              echo "mode-$pkg=junit" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            else
              echo "mode-$pkg=filecount" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          done

      # Skew is measured over WEIGHTS (summed meta.weights per shard — real
      # test durations once junit artifacts exist, file counts before), not
      # unit counts: counting units said nothing about balance (issue #194
      # pt 1). Units missing from weights (brand-new dirs) count as 1.0.
      # Both manifests are measured (core + fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Skew before rebalance
        id: before
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"skew-core={skew('scripts/test_shards.json')}")
          print(f"skew-faui={skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF

      - name: Run the rebalancer
        run: |
          # Core is file-level ×4 (test/cli was half the suite as a single
          # dir-unit — undivisible; see ci.yml test-core comment).
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-core }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit .timings-core \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          else
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          fi
          # fa_ui (issue #283): flat layout → file-level units; goldens are
          # host-locked and stay out of the shards. Units are stored
          # relative to packages/fa_ui (same convention as core's test/).
          cd packages/fa_ui
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-faui }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit ../../.timings-faui \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          else
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          fi

      # Commit only when a manifest was missing or the skew (max shard
      # size / mean shard size) strictly improved for EITHER suite (core
      # or fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Decide whether to commit
        id: decide
        run: |
          after=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

      # AC4 (REG): the checker must reject a @v4 fixture, a 40-char NON-hex
      # ref (mutable branch with a SHA-shaped name), and a nested composite
      # action manifest — and accept clean equivalents. A gate that cannot
      # fail is decoration.
      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad/bad.yml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@gggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggggg\n' > "$tmp/bad-hex/bad.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n' > "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          printf 'jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good/good.yml"
          printf 'name: probe\nruns:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v4\n' > "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep/action.yaml"
          # String-safety: a uses-shaped string INSIDE a run: scalar is not a
          # step ref — the checker is line-anchored (^[[:space:]]*(- )?uses:)
          # and must not flag it. (Regression: a reviewer suspected the
          # fixture printf lines in this very workflow would trip AC1.)
          printf "jobs:\n  probe:\n    steps:\n      - name: write fixture\n        run: |\n          printf 'jobs:\\\\n  probe:\\\\n    steps:\\\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\\\\n' > out.yml\n          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n" > "$tmp/string-safe/wf.yml"
          for bad in bad bad-hex bad-composite; do
            if bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::error::pin checker FAILED to flag the $bad fixture"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/good-composite" >/dev/null
          bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path "$tmp/string-safe" >/dev/null
          echo "fixture regression OK: @v4 / 40-char non-hex / unpinned nested composite rejected; SHA-pinned accepted; uses-shaped run-scalar strings ignored"

How to prepare a release

[!NOTE] Relevant for maintainers with write access only.

  1. Switch to a new branch from main.
  2. Run npm test to ensure all tests are passing.
  3. Update the version in https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/package.json.

  6. Run licensed cache to update the license report.
  7. Run licensed status and resolve any warnings by updating the https://github.com/actions/cache/blob/main/.licensed.yml file with the exceptions.
  8. Commit your changes and push your branch upstream.
  9. Open a pull request against main and get it reviewed and merged.
  10. Draft a new release https://github.com/actions/cache/releases use the same version number used in package.json
    1. Create a new tag with the version number.

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Example app pub get
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter pub get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The Chrome extension ships on the site too (download + load
      # unpacked): dart2js the SW agent and zip it — flutter is already on
      # PATH here and the script's --with-app embeds the same web build.
      - name: Build Chrome extension
        run: |
          dart pub get
          cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          cp -R site/. build/pages/root/
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5.0.1

blocks.text:
# Weekly test-shard rebalancer (issue #177, AC3/E4): re-splits the unit-test
# shards from downloaded JUnit timing artifacts when available (file counts
# otherwise) and commits scripts/test_shards.json back to main ONLY when the
# skew improved or the manifest was missing.
name: Shard rebalance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rebalance:
    name: Rebalance test shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # secrets.* is not allowed in job-level `if:`, so the PAT is exported as
    # an env var and the push step below skips itself gracefully when empty.
    env:
      RELEASE_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed manifest triggers downstream
          # workflows; an unset secret falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN here and the
          # push step skips itself.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      # Timing artifacts come from recent successful CI runs on main; their
      # absence is fine — the rebalancer then falls back to file counts.
      # Core (junit-shard-*) and fa_ui (junit-faui-shard-*, issue #283)
      # timings are split into separate dirs so same-named suite paths can
      # never cross-contaminate the other's weights.
      - name: Download recent JUnit timing artifacts (best effort)
        id: timings
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .shard-timings .timings-core .timings-faui
          for id in $(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main \
              --status success --limit 5 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
            gh run download "$id" --dir ".shard-timings/$id" \
              --pattern '*junit*' 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          find .shard-timings -name '*.xml' | while read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              *junit-faui-shard-*) cp "$f" ".timings-faui/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
              *junit-shard-*)      cp "$f" ".timings-core/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" ;;
            esac
          done
          for pkg in core faui; do
            if find ".timings-$pkg" -name '*.xml' -print -quit | grep -q .; then
              echo "mode-$pkg=junit" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            else
              echo "mode-$pkg=filecount" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            fi
          done

      # Skew is measured over WEIGHTS (summed meta.weights per shard — real
      # test durations once junit artifacts exist, file counts before), not
      # unit counts: counting units said nothing about balance (issue #194
      # pt 1). Units missing from weights (brand-new dirs) count as 1.0.
      # Both manifests are measured (core + fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Skew before rebalance
        id: before
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"skew-core={skew('scripts/test_shards.json')}")
          print(f"skew-faui={skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF

      - name: Run the rebalancer
        run: |
          # Core is file-level ×4 (test/cli was half the suite as a single
          # dir-unit — undivisible; see ci.yml test-core comment).
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-core }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit .timings-core \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          else
            python3 scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --shards 4
          fi
          # fa_ui (issue #283): flat layout → file-level units; goldens are
          # host-locked and stay out of the shards. Units are stored
          # relative to packages/fa_ui (same convention as core's test/).
          cd packages/fa_ui
          if [ "${{ steps.timings.outputs.mode-faui }}" = "junit" ]; then
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit ../../.timings-faui \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          else
            python3 ../../scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-filecount \
              --unit-style files --exclude golden \
              --output ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          fi

      # Commit only when a manifest was missing or the skew (max shard
      # size / mean shard size) strictly improved for EITHER suite (core
      # or fa_ui, issue #283).
      - name: Decide whether to commit
        id: decide
        run: |
          after=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json
          def skew(path):
              try:
                  m = json.load(open(path))
                  shards = m.get('shards', m) if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                  seq = shards.values() if isinstance(shards, dict) else shards
                  w = m.get('meta', {}).get('weights', {}) if isinstance(m, dict) else {}
                  loads = [sum(float(w.get(u, 1.0)) for u in s) for s in seq]
                  avg = sum(loads) / len(loads) if loads else 0
                  return max(loads) / avg if avg else 0
              except Exception:
                  return "missing"
          print(f"{skew('scripts/test_shards.json')} {skew('scripts/faui_test_shards.json')}")
          EOF
          )
          after_core=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f1)
          after_faui=$(echo "$after" | cut -d' ' -f2)
          before_core="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-core }}"
          before_faui="${{ steps.before.outputs.skew-faui }}"
          echo "skew core: before=$before_core after=$after_core"
          echo "skew faui: before=$before_faui after=$after_faui"
          improved() {
            [ "$1" = "missing" ] && return 0
            [ "$2" != "missing" ] && \
              awk -v a="$2" -v b="$1" 'BEGIN{exit !(a < b)}'
          }
          if improved "$before_core" "$after_core" || \
             improved "$before_faui" "$after_faui"; then
            echo "commit=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "commit=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Commit and push rebalanced manifest to main
        if: steps.decide.outputs.commit == 'true'
        run: |
          if [ -z "$RELEASE_PAT" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured; skipping push of shard manifests"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "418982+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add scripts/test_shards.json scripts/faui_test_shards.json
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Manifest unchanged; nothing to push."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(ci): rebalance test shards (issues #177, #283)"
          git push origin HEAD:main

      - name: AC4 — pin-checker fixture regression
        run: |
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$tmp/bad" "$tmp/bad-hex" "$tmp/bad-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/good" "$tmp/good-composite/.github/actions/probe/deep" "$tmp/string-safe"

  # SEC-08 (#796): audit BOTH dependency graphs. pubspec_overrides.yaml
  # redirects dart_tui to the vendored fork (vendor/dart_tui) for local/CI/
  # release builds while pubspec.yaml pins hosted dart_tui for the published
  # package — two different graphs; an audit of one says nothing about the
  # other. Each graph gets its own matrix leg and the split is documented in
  # the audit output.
  dep-audit:
    name: Dependency audit (${{ matrix.graph }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        graph: [hosted, vendored]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
